messages:
sam: Heads-up: DSAR from an EU user asking for full erasure + attestation. Primary erase returned success but long-term backups in backup-account:redwood-eu-retain still show copies under retention-exception. Need triage and proposal.
olga: Thanks. Which storage? EBS snapshots copied cross-account for long-retention policy or S3 objects?
ben: It's cross-account EBS snapshot copies used for vuln forensics. Snapshot IDs: snap-eu-1122, snap-eu-3344. They were copied to backup-account on 2026-02-28 with tag retention:exception=vuln-2026-11. Automation was supposed to clear after 30d but job failed.
lina-legal: For DSAR we must either fully delete or provide a lawful basis to retain. If this exception isn't valid now, we need to remove it and delete. Otherwise we must deliver a clear justification + expected retention end date and evidence of approvals.
sec-oncall: The exception was set by sec-oncall during emergent vulnerability triage (VULN-2026-11). The owner was @ben but I don't see the approval ticket in the retention tracker. Automation shows error: webhook 504 to tracker service.
audit-bot: CloudTrail: there is an anomaly — events for role snapshot-manager:CopySnapshot between 2026-02-28T03:00:00Z and 2026-02-28T03:20:00Z are present, but S3 and KMS logs for the copy show delayed ingestion. Some KMS:ReEncrypt events are missing due to the log-forwarder restart at 2026-03-01T02:15Z.
sam: Legal needs a defensible artifact chain. If we delete now, great. If we destroy KMS key material used by the backups, that is also destruction, but legal wants records showing the key schedule and who approved deletion.
ben: Technical constraints: the backup-account owns the snapshots and the KMS key is in that account (alias/backup-redwood-kms). We do not have cross-account decrypt rights. Options: 1) request backup-account to run deletion job; 2) request cross-account temporary AssumeRole to perform CopySnapshot->ReEncrypt->Delete; 3) schedule key destruction in backup-account.
olga: I'd prefer copy->re-encrypt->delete flow so we retain an artifact proving we scrubbed and kept a manifest. Key destruction may be simplest for privacy but eliminates ability to inspect contents later (for legal claims).
lina-legal: If you choose key destruction, we need notarized runbook entries: who initiated, timestamp, key schedule, and proof of no access after deletion. Without CloudTrail in one window we will need supporting evidence (session recordings, PR approvals).
sec-oncall: Quick fix: we can perform an in-place quarantine: restrict snapshot ACLs, tag sar:case=EU-DSAR-2026-77, and open a limited-time recovery window for legal to request forensics. Then run cross-account copy->re-encrypt using a temp key we control, verify content hash, then delete the copied snapshot and schedule temp key deletion. That gives an artifact chain in our account.
ben: That requires an RBAC change: snapshot-manager role will need sts:AssumeRole -> backup-admin for up to 2 hours. I can open a PR for the scoped permission (ec2:CopySnapshot, ec2:DeleteSnapshot, kms:Encrypt, kms:ReEncrypt, kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion) with timebound conditions.
olga: Keep the session ephemeral and record it. Use session tags: sar=EU-DSAR-2026-77 and include approver.
sam: Lina, do you approve ephemeral access by our erasure-runner to the backup-account for this DSAR?
lina-legal: Approve ephemeral access for the explicit purpose described. Require: recorded session, PR diff, and upload of all CLI output to /legal/sar-evidence/EU-DSAR-2026-77. If there is any missing CloudTrail, include node-level syslogs and s3 access logs.
sec-oncall: audit-bot, please pull available logs and generate an evidence bundle with checksums.
audit-bot: Evidence bundle generated (partial): /tmp/evidence/EU-DSAR-2026-77/preliminary-bundle.tar.gz. Note: missing KMS events between 2026-02-28T03:05 and 2026-02-28T03:10 UTC due to forwarder restart. Node syslogs cover 03:02-03:12 and show aws-kms-daemon start/stop messages.
ben: Plan I'll propose in PR: 1) Create timebound AssumeRole via ephemeral policy; 2) Copy snap-eu-1122 -> to our account with alias/redwood-kms-temp; 3) Verify checksum and manifest; 4) Run erasure pipeline against copied snapshot; 5) Delete copied snapshot and schedule temp key deletion; 6) Push artifact bundle to legal.
olga: Also create a mitigation memo explaining why automation failed and update retention automation to alert on webhook errors.
sam: Action owners: ben (run copy + delete), olga (RBAC PR + session control), sec-oncall (assist + logging), lina-legal (accept artifacts). Timeline: start in next 6 hours, aim to close DSAR within statutory window.
lina-legal: Confirmed. If the backup-account refuses cross-account access, we will escalate to backup-account owners and consider key schedule deletion as last resort, but record decision memo.
ben: I'll draft the PR now and include least-privilege policy. Will post session start and end here.
audit-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/infra/pr/4567 (policy + justification).
olga: Approving PR per scope, will require sec+legal ack.
sec-oncall: Starting ephemeral session in 10m and will record.
ben: copy started for snap-eu-1122 using alias/redwood-kms-temp. CLI output logged.
sam: remember to tag copy with sar=EU-DSAR-2026-77 and include source snapshot manifest in artifact.
audit-bot: copy job completed, checksum match OK for snap-eu-1122. Second snapshot queued.
ben: second snapshot done too. Running erasure pipeline now.
sec-oncall: session recorded: s3://audit-recordings/sessions/EU-DSAR-2026-77/session-7891.rec (access-limited).
lina-legal: Once artifacts are uploaded, legal will package attestation letter with manifest and timeline. Keep PR and session logs.
ben: artifacts uploaded: s3://legal/sar-evidence/EU-DSAR-2026-77/bundle-v1.tar.gz (manifest, CLI logs, session recording, PR diff).
sam: follow-up: create runbook update to surface retention-exception drift. Filing ticket INFRA-2026-442.
olga: Will also add periodic audit to ensure retention exceptions have manual owner and auto-expiry checks.
sec-oncall: Closing loop: automation remediation scheduled and RBAC change reverted after session.
lina-legal: Good. Legal to respond to DSAR with attestation and mitigation note for the missing logs.
audit-bot: thread closed pending any escalation.
